brief: Meta's Muse agentic-AI app, live in the US, triggers a broad risk-on rotation into AI infrastructure. META has its best day in 17 months, up 17% over 9 sessions, and the CPU complex (ARM, Intel, AMD, Qualcomm) rallies as investors connect agentic workflows to heavier CPU and inference demand, with AMD crossing $1tn market cap. Sister app Instinct reaches over 100k users in three weeks, with its private valuation reportedly moving from $2.25B toward a targeted $10B. Muse's early US download and daily-user numbers reportedly outpace ChatGPT's early launch. This creates a split read-through. Infrastructure, security and agent-enabler names benefit, while transaction-heavy marketplaces face disintermediation risk, tracked in GS's Muse/Instinct At-Risk Basket (GSXUSWCH). Shopify rallies on an agentic-checkout tie-up with Muse, while Amazon blocks Muse from its storefront. Tencent and Alibaba escalate competing AI models and chips in China. Elsewhere, Infineon flags supportive AI power-semi pricing and a debate over guide upside, South Korea's chip-led export surplus hits a record, Apple's foldable iPhone faces assembly-yield risk, Sunrise reviews up to 450 job cuts, and US equities and oil move on Trump-Xi summit optimism, with asset managers net buyers and hedge funds net sellers.
